story_type: sailboat aground against a rock wall in surf, boat crew tows it clear
hook: Four people aboard, pinned against a rock wall by the surf.
narration: Four people were on this sailboat, pinned against a rock wall by the surf.
The thirty six foot sailboat had run aground at the south end of Lopez Island, Washington.
At about ten past five in the evening, they called the Coast Guard for help.
Waves kept breaking white over the rocks, right beside the hull.
A boat crew from Station Bellingham drove straight in alongside, almost touching the rocks.
In surge like this, a rescue boat has to keep its engines working the whole time, or the next wave can push it onto the rocks too.
A crewman got a line across to the sailboat and made it fast.
[short pause] Then the Coast Guard boat backed away, and the line went tight.
outcome: The Coast Guard crew towed the sailboat off the rocks and out into open water.
title: Sailboat pinned against a rock wall
description:
On May 27, 2007, a 36-foot sailboat with four people aboard ran aground at the south end of Lopez Island, Washington. A Coast Guard Station Bellingham boat crew came alongside in the surf and towed it clear, filmed from an Air Station Port Angeles helicopter.
